title: Joint family and series screens reduced error and large losses in 16 climate-response families
abstract: We tested the joint use of two published training-only climate-response screens. We reused signed model statistics for 32,733 series in 16 families, with models fitted through 2004 and later tests from 2005. Climate was used only when a family false-signal rate was at most 0.32 and a series had cross-validated signal at least 0.10 with null-tail ratio at most 0.20. Equal-family mean error reduction, normalized by each old training-mean error, was 0.14666 for the joint rule, 0.13577 for the series screen and 0.13309 for the family screen. The share with more than double the trailing-mean error fell from 2.96% for the series screen to 0.65% for joint use. The rule still lost for German crop timing. In five families with a newer trend-preserving null, joint use reduced observed harm but gave no clear mean gain over the trend family gate: 0.00074, with conditional 95% limits of -0.00160 to 0.00388. We retained 34 nonfinite trailing-baseline skill ratios by using finite additive loss differences. These are retrospective model-statistic results, not new field records or forecasts made before weather was known. Shared time uncertainty and selection after initial outcome inspection limit inference. Code, hashes, aggregate results and independent checks are supplied.

display.caption: Equal-family mean gain and frequency of harm. The joint rule requires both family and series screens. Full use, series screening and joint screening use the same source model statistics.
